title: SJD-SV: Speculative Jacobi Decoding with Semantics Verification for Autoregressive Image Generation
claim: Token-by-token verification rejects ambiguous fine-grained tokens early; verifying semantic subsequences accepts more tokens per step.
layout: 2 stacked sections: top token-ambiguity visualization, bottom left-vs-right method comparison
description: The figure has two parts. Panel (a), at the top, shows a photo of a Shiba Inu in a patterned scarf. A blue arrow labeled 'Token' leads to a copy of the photo overlaid with a 48×48 grid. Red dashed lines run from six grid cells to magnified patches of fur, scarf and background texture. These patches are small and unclear, which illustrates token ambiguity. Panel (b), at the bottom, compares two pipelines side by side. The left pipeline, 'Existing SJD Methods', sends colored draft-token circles through a blue Token Verification Step. The tokens get sequential green accept checks until the first red reject, and then all the remaining tokens are rejected and resampled. Only three tokens are accepted. The right pipeline, 'Our SJD-SV', uses peach boxes. It partitions the draft tokens into three dashed-outline subsequences and verifies each subsequence as a unit. Six tokens are accepted in the end. The eye goes first to the dog photo, then to the red crosses and checks.
caption: (a) Existing image AR models represents an image as a fine-grained token sequence, such that individual tokens is difficult to accurately and clearly express a certain semantic, thereby introducing token ambiguity; (b) Instead of performing token-by-token verification as existing SJD methods, we turn to perform verification on semantic-aware token subsequence level. Its advantage is that token subsequences can encode more stable semantic information, effectively reducing false rejections during verification.
abstract: Speculative Jacobi Decoding (SJD) is an important approach for accelerating autoregressive image generation. Although SJD has shown superior performance, recent studies point out that it usually suffers from a token ambiguity issue during token verification but its reason can not be well explained. To figure out this reason, in this paper, we conduct a visualization analysis on vision token and find that different from text tokens, vision tokens generally corresponds to some local, small, and unclear vision details, which means only using single token is difficult to accurately express a certain semantic, thereby causing token ambiguity issue. To this end, we propose a novel Speculative Jacobi Decoding with Semantics Verification (called SJD-SV), for accelerating autoregressive image generation. The key idea is that leveraging the strong correction characters between tokens to recognize semantic-aware token subsequence and then instead of perform token-by-token verification, turning to perform verification on semantic-aware token subsequence level for accelerating image generation. In particular, our method is plug-in, which can be directly integrated into existing SJD and its variants. Extensive experiments on various datasets show that existing SJD methods achieve significant performance improvement after integrating our SJD-SV method.
